**Exact target:** Every sufficiently large original planar unit-separated EXACT
UNRESTRICTED GLOBAL diameter minimizer contains an ORIGINAL unit equilateral
triangle. **Still OPEN.** This file integrates worker proposals after ROOT
logical checking. Full, unmodified worker responses are
\`work/erdos99/w99_933..938_*.result.json\`; their immutable original
submission receipts remain beside them. No publication or historical novelty
claim is made.

## Native Aquinas: optimized same-n replacement-area necessary condition

Native GPT-6 Sol Web High Aquinas \`01a1892c-15e6-7860-8973-13d674c6429a\`,
COMPLETED/CLOSED on 2026-10-29. Independently refereed the already
ROOT-corrected general lemma in canonical section 272. Let X be an original
global n-point diameter minimizer of diameter D. Choose an ORIGINAL diameter
edge vertex cover R, of cardinality k, and U=X\\R; then diam(U)<D
(when |U|>=2). For every d<D and closed disk B(c,d/2), define

\`Omega(d,c)=B(c,d/2) intersection_{u in U}{z: 1<=|z-u|<=d}\`.

If k original replacement sites could be found with unit mutual distances
or larger inside Omega, together with retained U they would beat D; hence
\`pack_1(Omega)<=k-1\`. The translate-average of the unit triangular
lattice (fundamental area sqrt(3)/2) yields
\`area(Omega)<=(k-1)sqrt(3)/2\` (for k>=2). k=1 requires Omega empty;
k=2 also implies diam(Omega)<1 and hence area(Omega)<=pi/4.
No assumption U subset B is legitimate or required; BOTH lower and upper
cross-distance constraints must be retained. Earlier section 272 proves a
strict finite-d version; the non-strict version suffices here.

Aquinas' useful reformulation is \`F_D(U)=intersection_{u in U}
{z:1<=|z-u|<=D}\` and
\`M_R(X)=sup_c area(F_D(U) intersect B(c,D/2))\`.
Monotone area convergence as d tends upward to D gives
\`M_R(X)<=(k-1)sqrt(3)/2\`, also \`M_R(X)<=pi/4\` for k=2.
This condition is necessary for EVERY original exact-global optimizer.
The missing theorem would be a strictly larger lower bound on M_R for
some diameter cover R in every large original triangle-free global optimizer.
No such theorem is proved. Increasing R relaxes geometric constraints but
also raises the comparison threshold; no free contradiction follows.
Aquinas checked the original exact-global unit square n=4 has nonempty
replacement region, so triangle-freeness does not force emptiness.
Background: Erdős 1994
https://mathematica-pannonica.ttk.pte.hu/articles/mp05-2/mp05-2-261-269.pdf ;
Oler 1961 https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1961-018-7 .

## Original WebAgentGPT w99_933: sparse, positively stressed near-global countermodel

Immutable public research job \`73cbdd97-eacf-40f5-be80-6bce1537ee30\`
COMPLETED/SAVED. For growing odd m, regular unit-side m-gon vertices
\`v_j=R(cos(2pi j/m),sin(2pi j/m))\`, \`R=1/(2sin(pi/m))\`,
plus inner sites of (1+1/m)-scaled unit triangular lattice within radius
\`R-sqrt(R)\`, give n~(2pi/sqrt(3))R^2, exactly m original unit
contacts (the polygon cycle), no original unit triangle, and original
diameter \`2R cos(pi/(2m))\` for large m. All original contacts and
diametral edges admit strictly positive KKT weights
\`lambda=D^2/m\`, \`mu=1/m\` respectively; interior sites have
zero forces. Oler proves \`diam(A_m)/D_{n_m}->1\`. A COMPETING
unit triangular-lattice disk of radius \`R-sqrt(R)/2\` contains at
least n_m points for all large m and has smaller diameter. Thus these
are rigorously NON-GLOBAL. Claim checked at asymptotic/logical level;
full construction proof and equations are preserved in its raw result.
No KKT or asymptotic-tightness-to-contact-count implication holds in
this generality. Oler: https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1961-018-7 .

## Original WebAgentGPT w99_934: block gluing fails on explicit family

Original job \`7bfd9e26-8142-40f1-ae80-2afae39a2d40\`
COMPLETED/SAVED. For kxk unit-heptagon-plus-center blocks translated
by (4p,4q), the 8k^2 original sites are separated, triangle-free,
and have diameter >=4sqrt(2)(k-1). A 4k by 2k staggered unit
triangular-lattice rectangle gives a same-cardinality unrestricted
competitor of squared diameter <=19k^2-7k+1. For all k>=4,
\`32(k-1)^2 > 19k^2-7k+1\`, since
\`13k^2-57k+31>0\`. Thus those exact, infinite triangle-free
BLOCK unions are provably NON-GLOBAL for k>=4. No ruling about all
possible glued motif designs follows. n8 original-global source:
Bezdek-Fodor https://doi.org/10.1006/jcta.1998.2889 .

## Original WebAgentGPT w99_935: cubic-order strict descent barrier

Original job \`dbecd4ee-0d32-459d-baaa-fd31d3d17335\`
COMPLETED/SAVED. A six-ORIGINAL-site deformation of the regular unit
hexagon with A(s)=1-s^3, a=sqrt(3)(1-s)/2, b=(1+3s)/2,
h=a-sqrt(A(s)^(-2)-b^2), positions
\`p0=A(1+s,h)\`,
\`pk=A(1+(-1)^k*s)(cos(k*pi/3),sin(k*pi/3)), k=1..5\`
has min distance exactly 1, and
\`diam^2=A^2(4+h^2)=4-8s^3+3s^4+O(s^5)<4\`
for small s>0. First and second derivatives of squared diameter
along this feasible path are zero; cubic-order decrease is strict.
Importantly, this same direction already fails a full second-order
KKT necessary condition, so it does NOT show second-order KKT is
insufficient as a complete test. It is a nonglobal regular-hexagon
example and has no exact-global triangle consequence. Compared with
earlier independently checked Wave92 hexagon perturbation.

## Original WebAgentGPT w99_936: rational n=9 upper certificate, NO global certificate

Original job \`1f9d5852-28c4-437b-83f8-1d8d28efbc52\`
COMPLETED/SAVED. Integer Cartesian coordinates for 9 original sites
and exact 36 squared-distance computations appear in the raw result.
Reported unique minimum squared integer gap
\`Qmin=151522591800822877\` at pair (1,3) and unique max
\`Qmax=1000197395492102464\` at (7,8), giving rational witness
\`D9<=sqrt(Qmax/Qmin)<2.569236981\`.
A tiny rational move of site 7 toward site 8 keeps pair (1,3) shortest
and strictly reduces the longest pair; the published precision-shape
is not locally optimal. This does not determine D9. This record is
consistent with earlier verified n9 bounds, though the NEW independent
executable check \`audit-wave99-new.py\` was not executed because
the runtime blocked that audit call. Source of original candidate:
https://minmaxarena.com/en/problems/min-distance-ratio/p52-n9-v1 ;
original finite global n8: https://doi.org/10.1006/jcta.1998.2889 .

## Original WebAgentGPT w99_937: no full-hull GWZ equality for large optima

Original job \`cab841e5-20a1-4278-bd22-4d12d9dfd1cf\`
COMPLETED/SAVED proposed a direct proof for n>=2500. If full-hull
Oler/GWZ slack tau=0, the ORIGINAL sites support an all-unit
equilateral triangulation and hence embed in one triangular lattice.
The convex hull is a convex polygon with at most SIX genuine corners
(six lattice directions). The existing project-internal ROOT-audited
finite ORIGINAL global hull-vertex lower bound in canonical section
259 says \`m^2 >= [5pi^2/(12sqrt(3))] D_n\`, where m counts
original hull extreme vertices. Thus for tau=0,
\`D_n <= 36*12sqrt(3)/(5pi^2) = 15.1626330390...\`.
Oler with A<=pi D^2/4, P<=pi D yields
\`n <= pi D_n^2/(2sqrt(3)) + (pi/2)D_n +1
     <=233.3185793481...\`.
ROOT therefore derives the stronger conditional corollary:
**For every n>=234 and EVERY original exact-global minimizer,
full-hull Oler/GWZ slack is positive.** The numerical constants were
independently evaluated via local Python; this deduction depends
on the project-internal rigor of section 259 and its former audits,
not a published theorem. Note this is an incompatibility with FULL
GWZ equality, NOT an exclusion of local original unit triangles.
GWZ 1972 https://doi.org/10.2140/pjm.1972.41.699 ;
Oler https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1961-018-7 .

## Original WebAgentGPT w99_938: primary-source status and quantifier referee

Original job \`38023ca0-d8cd-4d3f-ab7b-d8d3ac3cb44b\`

limits of Oler, GWZ and September 2026 Das preprint. It found no

https://www.erdosproblems.com/99 . Original Erdős:
https://mathematica-pannonica.ttk.pte.hu/articles/mp05-2/mp05-2-261-269.pdf ;
Das preprint https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22768362 .

Original public w99_932 area-window job
\`0cb3a91a-95ac-4838-83d4-bf1b4bee8dc4\` was

Ramanujan \`01a18939-9106-72e1-ae1f-273563fe0343\`;
Pauli \`01a18939-a4ef-7143-8eef-b1f99d19a81b\`;
Halley \`01a18939-ad2a-7612-a764-f16b8f3afb61\`.
All three are independent research-only checks, no local writes.
The all-original, all-exact-global sufficiently-large Erdős #99
remains OPEN. No external publication, GitHub change, PR or outreach.
"""

# A global boundary zigzag competitor with a linear population reserve

**Classification:** proved candidate awaiting promotion; **unreviewed**.
**Level I remains open.**

Baseline `ab6dd3336f9f8d440f2bada76edb32153391cddc`, state
`2026-10-10.audit.234`; independent branch
`research/sol/global-independent-20261011`.

## 1. Statement and global implication

Write `a0=sqrt(3)/2` and `a=pi/(2sqrt(3))`. For every real
`R>=640000`, there exists a unit-separated set in the closed radius-`R` disk
with cardinality at least

\[
\boxed{{\pi R^2\over a_0}+{R\over160000}.}
\tag{1}
\]

More precisely, **every translate** of the triangular lattice, cropped to this
disk, admits the explicitly described boundary replacement gaining at least
`R/160000` points. Translation averaging then supplies (1).

Consequently every global minimum-diameter `n`-point unit-separated source with
`D>1280000` satisfies

\[
\boxed{g_A:=n-1-aD^2\ge {D\over320000}.}
\tag{2}
\]

The implication chain is

```text
simultaneous boundary replacements in a whole lattice disk
  -> a full-source independent competitor with linear extra population
  -> the global-minimizer population reserve (2).
```

The construction does not move a hypothetical minimizer or identify it with a
lattice. It constructs a separate configuration of controlled diameter, then
uses global optimality only for the cardinality comparison. It retains all
labels of a hypothetical source in that comparison. This is a global population
result, not a triangle theorem or a C-II finite-motion theorem.

## 2. One row replacement, including the complete pair ledger

Use the triangular lattice

\[
\Lambda_t=\{t+(j+k/2,ka_0):j,k\in\mathbb Z\}.
\]

Let `y=t_y+ka0>0` be one row height. Suppose an interval `[A,B]`, with integer
endpoints and length `L=B-A`, has these two properties in the disk:

1. `(x,y+1/2)` lies in the disk for every `x in [A,B]`;
2. no retained lattice point of a higher row has horizontal coordinate in
   `(A,B)`.

Delete exactly the row-`y` lattice points whose horizontal coordinates lie in
`[A,B]`. There are at most `L+1` of them, irrespective of translation or row
parity. Set `h=19/20`, and insert

\[
p_i=(A+1+ih,\ y+\eta_i),\qquad
0\le i\le\left\lfloor{L-2\over h}\right\rfloor,
\]

where `eta_i=1/6` for even `i` and `eta_i=1/2` for odd `i`.

All the pair checks are explicit:

- Adjacent inserted points have squared distance
  `h^2+(1/3)^2=3649/3600>1`.
- Nonadjacent inserted points have horizontal separation at least `2h=19/10>1`.
- Every lower lattice row has vertical separation at least
  `a0+1/6>1` from every inserted point.
- Retained points on the same row lie outside `[A,B]`, hence have horizontal
  separation at least one and positive vertical separation.
- Higher retained rows have horizontal coordinates outside `(A,B)`, so have
  horizontal separation at least one and positive vertical separation.
- Inserted points stay in the disk: they are above the positive row `y`, below
  its height `y+1/2`, and at horizontal coordinates in `[A,B]`.

Thus every new-involving lower distance is in fact strict. Old retained pairs
keep their original lower bound. No assertion about a stress or a local
linearization is used.

The net cardinality gain is at least

\[
{L-2\over h}-(L+1)={L-59\over19}.
\tag{3}
\]

For `L>64`, the integer gain is therefore at least one.

## 3. Simultaneously available rows on a shallow circular arc

Set `delta=1/200` and `f(x)=sqrt(R^2-x^2)`. Work only in the upper-right
arc with horizontal coordinate between `delta R/2` and `delta R`.
Choose every lattice row `y` such that

\[
f(\delta R)\le y,
\qquad y+a_0\le f(\delta R/2).
\tag{4}
\]

Define real endpoints and their inward integer roundings by

\[
u_y=\sqrt{R^2-(y+a_0)^2},\qquad
v_y=\sqrt{R^2-(y+1/2)^2},\qquad
A_y=\lceil u_y\rceil,\quad B_y=\lfloor v_y\rfloor.
\tag{5}
\]

For `x in [A_y,B_y]`, the disk top is at least `y+1/2` and at most
`y+a0`. Equality at the left endpoint is harmless because of the one-unit
horizontal guard used by the packet. Thus both hypotheses of Section 2 hold.

Throughout these intervals,

\[
\left|{d\over dz}\sqrt{R^2-z^2}\right|
={z\over\sqrt{R^2-z^2}}
\ge {\sqrt{1-\delta^2}\over\delta}>199.
\]

Since `a0-1/2>1/3`, the mean value theorem and rounding give

\[
v_y-u_y>{199\over3},\qquad
L_y=B_y-A_y>{199\over3}-2={193\over3}>64.
\tag{6}
\]

Each selected row therefore gains at least one point.

The intervals for different rows are disjoint: their corresponding height
intervals `[y+1/2,y+a0]` are disjoint, and `z -> sqrt(R^2-z^2)` is
strictly decreasing here. Integer rounding only shrinks the intervals. Every
packet stays one unit inside each of its interval endpoints. Two packets on
different rows consequently have horizontal separation at least two. The row
replacements are **simultaneously** feasible, and they delete disjoint sets of
old labels. This checks the cross-packet constraints, not just single-row moves.

Let

\[
\Delta=f(\delta R/2)-f(\delta R).
\]

The number `K` of rows satisfying (4), for any vertical lattice translation,
obeys

\[
K\ge {\Delta\over a_0}-2\ge\Delta-2.
\tag{7}
\]

Rationalizing the difference of square roots gives

\[
\Delta
={3\delta^2R/4\over
\sqrt{1-\delta^2/4}+\sqrt{1-\delta^2}}
\ge {3\delta^2R\over8}={3R\over320000}.
\]

For `R>=640000`, equations (7) therefore give

\[
K\ge {3R\over320000}-2\ge {R\over160000}.
\tag{8}
\]

The untouched bulk, the remaining boundary rows, and all the packets form one
unit-separated packing in the original disk. This proves the claimed gain for
every translated lattice crop.

## 4. Averaging and the strict global comparison

Average `|Lambda_t cap B(0,R)|` over one fundamental parallelogram. The mean is
`pi R^2/a0`; some translate has at least that many points. Apply the construction
to that translate and use (8), proving (1).

Now suppose an `n`-point global minimizer has diameter `D>1280000`. For every
`640000<=R<D/2`, (1) supplies a packing of some integer cardinality `N_R` and
diameter at most `2R<D`. If `N_R>=n`, any `n`-point subset contradicts global
optimality. Therefore

\[
n-1\ge N_R\ge {\pi R^2\over a_0}+{R\over160000}.
\]

Take `R` up to `D/2`. The right side is continuous, so (2) follows. This limiting
step preserves the strict smaller-diameter comparison: each individual
competitor used before the limit has diameter strictly below `D`.

The construction proves existence of a separate competitor, with its entire
lower and upper pair ledger checked. It does not assume a source lattice frame,
a supplied train family, stress-weight lower bounds, or any omitted-label bound.

## 5. Why this does not by itself settle Level I

The new reserve is linear in `D`; a source-specific upper estimate
`g_A=o(D)` for normalized triangle-free global minimizers would now suffice.
Such an upper estimate has **not** been proved here.

It cannot hold for arbitrary triangle-free unit-separated sources. Fix any
`0<c<1/320000`. In the construction above choose `R<D/2` sufficiently close
to `D/2` that the resulting count is at least `aD^2+cD`. Then apply
`(x,y)->(x,(1+epsilon)y)` for a sufficiently small positive `epsilon` so
`2R(1+epsilon)<D`. All distances weakly increase, and a distance can remain
one only for a horizontal pair. Thus the new contact graph is a disjoint union
of horizontal paths and is triangle-free. The untouched central lattice region
contains horizontal unit pairs, so the minimum distance is still exactly one.
The cardinality is unchanged and the diameter is still strictly below `D`.

This accompanying **regression** rules out a triangle-free-only `o(D)` upper
bound. A closing bound must use the exact global-minimizer hypotheses. The
construction does not claim its triangle-free deformations are globally optimal.

This candidate awaits independent audit. It is not a promotion, a Level I

# Global joint diameter-cover exchange

**Classification:** proved candidate awaiting promotion; unreviewed, noncanonical.
**Level I:** open. The supplied-packet criterion below is proved; the universal
existence of a successful packet for large triangle-free minimizers is not proved.

## 1. State and endpoint

- Base commit: `ab6dd3336f9f8d440f2bada76edb32153391cddc`.
- State version: `2026-10-10.audit.234`.
- Route: whole-problem simultaneous source replacement, independent of A/B/C
  stress, phase, wall, or lattice hypotheses.
- Canonical dependency: `docs/problem/statement.md`, the definition of D(n) and
  its every-global-minimizer quantifier. The finite graph identities used below
  are proved here.
- Endpoint: construct at least n unit-separated points of diameter strictly
  below the diameter D of the complete n-label source.

The new implication chain is

`joint cover/matching cost <= comparison population`

`-> simultaneous mixed packet of at least n labels`

`-> strict-D competitor -> contradiction to global optimality`.

This is an exact finite equivalence for a supplied comparison packet. It does
not assume that independently feasible exchanges can be combined.

## 2. Exact full-source theorem

Let A=(a_1,...,a_n) be any finite unit-separated planar source of diameter D>0.
Let B=(b_1,...,b_m) be any finite unit-separated comparison packet with
diam(B)<D. Labels in the two families are distinct even if their coordinates
coincide.

Define the actual diameter graph H on the A labels by

    ij in H  iff  |a_i-a_j|=D.

Define the bipartite cross-conflict graph G between A and B by

    (i,j) in G  iff  |a_i-b_j|<1 or |a_i-b_j|>=D.

The second condition includes equality: the target diameter is strictly below
D. For a vertex cover T of H, let nu_T be the maximum matching size in the
bipartite graph G restricted to (A\T) union B. Put

    K(A,B) = min_{T covers H} (|T| + nu_T).

**Theorem.** The largest cardinality of a unit-separated, strict-D subset of
the labeled union A union B is exactly

    n + m - K(A,B).

In particular, this union supplies a strict-D competitor of source cardinality
if and only if there is a diameter vertex cover T with

    m - |T| - nu_T >= 0.                         (E)

If A is globally diameter minimizing, then for every such B and every cover T,

    |T| + nu_T >= m+1,                          (G)

equivalently nu_T >= m-|T|+1. All source isolates participate in G and in nu_T;
none are discarded.

### Proof of the finite matching identity

For completeness, a finite bipartite graph with parts L,R has minimum vertex
cover size equal to maximum matching size nu. A cover must meet every edge of
a matching and therefore has size at least nu.

Choose a maximum matching M. Starting at unmatched L vertices, traverse
unmatched edges from L to R and matched edges from R to L. Write Z_L,Z_R for
the reached vertices. No unmatched R vertex is reached: a shortest alternating
path to one would augment M. Every reached R vertex is matched to a reached
L vertex, and every reached matched L vertex is matched to a reached R vertex.
Thus

    (L\Z_L) union Z_R

has exactly nu vertices. It covers every edge. Indeed, an uncovered edge would
join l in Z_L to r outside Z_R. If the edge is unmatched, the traversal reaches
r. If it is matched, a reached matched l was reached through precisely that
matched edge, so r was already reached. Both cases contradict r outside Z_R.
This proves the identity and constructs the cover.

### Proof of the geometric theorem

Fix a cover T of H and forbid using its source labels. Within A\T, all distances
are at least 1 and strictly below D. Within B they have the same property by
hypothesis. A mixed subset is feasible precisely when it is an independent
set of the remaining bipartite cross-conflict graph. The complement of an
independent set is a vertex cover, so the maximum feasible cardinality for this
fixed T is

    n-|T|+m-nu_T.

Every term is attained by the matching-cover construction above. Conversely,
for any feasible subset of A union B, its omitted source labels form a cover
of H. Thus optimizing over covers T gives exactly the displayed formula.

If (E) holds, select any n labels of the resulting feasible subset. No two
selected labels have coincident coordinates, because coincidence is a lower
cross conflict. Their coordinates are a unit-separated n-point set of diameter
strictly below D. Global optimality forbids (E); integrality gives (G). QED.

### Useful equivalent Hall form

For a fixed T, the bipartite matching identity also gives

    m-nu_T = max_{S subset B} (|S|-|N_{A\T}(S)|).

Here the empty S is allowed. To check this identity directly, a matching can
match at most |N(S)| of S, giving one inequality. For the minimum cover
constructed above, take S=Z_L when L=B; its neighbors are exactly Z_R, and
|Z_L|-|Z_R| equals the number of unmatched B vertices.

Consequently (E) is precisely the existence of one *simultaneously compatible*
comparison subpacket S whose gain over its remaining source blockers pays
the forced diameter deletion |T|.

### Why only inclusion-minimal covers need be searched

If T subset T' are covers, deleting k=|T'\T| additional source vertices lowers
maximum matching size by at most k. Therefore

    |T'|+nu_T' >= |T|+nu_T.

Every cover contains an inclusion-minimal cover. An inclusion-minimal cover
contains no H-isolated source label. This observation reduces the forced
cover search; it does not remove any isolate from the matching calculation
or from the constructed packet. Minimum-*cardinality* covers alone are not
sufficient, as the next regression shows.

## 3. Exact geometric regressions

Every coordinate below is rational, and the verifier checks all pairs.

### 3.1 A nonminimum diameter cover can be essential

Take

    A = {(0,0), (-1/2,1), (1/2,1)},   D^2=5/4,
    B = {(-1/2,9/10), (1/2,9/10)}.

The source contact graph has just the edge between the two upper labels.
The bottom label is contact isolated. The actual diameter graph is the
two-edge star centered at (0,0).

Its unique minimum-cardinality cover removes the bottom label. Both comparison
labels have lower conflicts with their corresponding retained upper labels,
so nu_T=2 and m-|T|-nu_T=-1: that cover yields no competitor.

The other inclusion-minimal cover removes both upper labels. The retained
bottom label has squared distance 53/50 from each comparison label, which is
in [1,5/4). Hence nu_T=0 and m-|T|-nu_T=0. The mixed three-point competitor
has diameter squared 53/50<5/4. This source is explicitly nonglobal.

**Regression:** optimizing the minimum diameter-cover cardinality before
considering lower blockers is invalid, even with an actual star diameter
graph, a one-contact triangle-free source, and a lower-conflict graph that
is a matching.

### 3.2 A smaller comparison packet can augment the source

Take

    A = {(0,0),(2,0),(0,1),(2,1)},   D^2=5,
    B = {(1/2,0),(3/2,0),(1,1)}.

Delete the two bottom source labels. They cover both actual diameter pairs.
No comparison label conflicts with either retained top source label, so
nu_T=0. Although m=3<n=4, their union gives five unit-separated labels
of diameter squared 4<5. This is a certified simultaneous replacement,
including the inactive source and cross pairs. The source is nonglobal.

### 3.3 A known global source rejects the supplied packet

For the unit square A and

    B = {(0,1/10),(1,1/10),(1/2,11/10)},

the exact formula and exhaustive enumeration both give maximum mixed
cardinality 3, hence max_T(m-|T|-nu_T)=-1. The supplied packet cannot improve
the four-label source. This is a check on the strict inequality and integer
threshold, not a general packet-existence theorem.

### 3.4 Upper cross conflicts cannot be omitted

Translate the preceding B ten units to the right. It still has minimum
separation at least 1 and diameter squared 5/4<2. All twelve source/comparison
cross pairs have distance at least D, so G contains K_(4,3). The true maximum
mixed cardinality is 3. Keeping only lower conflicts incorrectly predicts
five labels after deleting a two-label source diameter cover.

**Regression:** the full cross-conflict graph is not generally planar and
cannot be replaced by the local unit-blocker graph.

## 4. Lower-conflict geometry

The graph with only the edges |a_i-b_j|<1 has a planar straight-line drawing,
up to the harmless separation of coincident source/comparison pairs.

Suppose two edges a-b and a'-b' meet in their relative interiors at x. Unit
separation within each family and the triangle inequality give

    1 <= |a-a'| <= |a-x|+|x-a'|,
    1 <= |b-b'| <= |b-x|+|x-b'|.

Adding them gives 2<=|a-b|+|a'-b'|<2, a contradiction. No edge interior can
contain another vertex: its same-family endpoint would then be less than
1 from that vertex. A coincident cross-family pair has no other lower-conflict
neighbor, by separation in the two families, and is an isolated edge.

Every lower-conflict vertex has degree at most five. Otherwise six opposite
family points in its open unit disk have a consecutive angular gap at most
pi/3. For radii r,s<1 their squared distance is at most r^2+s^2-r*s<1:
the last inequality follows by maximizing this separately convex expression
on the closed unit square, whose maximum is 1, and checking strictness when
r,s<1. A coincident opposite-family point excludes all other neighbors.
This contradicts their unit separation.

These properties apply to the full conflict graph only under an additional
strict upper-clearance condition, such as B being contained in every open
radius-D ball centered at a source point. That condition is not automatic.

## 5. Unbounded dense regression against minimum-cover-first search

The three-label obstruction is not a small-population phenomenon. The following
family has the triangular leading population coefficient, retains every
contact-isolated label, has exactly one unit contact, and has a full cross
graph that is merely a matching. It is explicitly nonglobal.

**Regression theorem.** For every integer k>=4 there are rational-coordinate
triangle-free sources A_k and packets B_k with D=k^2 and

    |A_k| = pi*D^2/(2*sqrt(3)) + O(D),
    |B_k| = |A_k|-1,

such that the unique minimum-cardinality diameter cover has exchange profit
-1, but an inclusion-minimal k-label diameter cover has profit 0 and produces
a same-cardinality competitor of diameter exactly D-1/8. The source has
exactly |A_k|-2 contact-isolated labels. The comparison cross graph, including
both upper and lower conflicts, is exactly a matching of size |B_k|.

### Complete construction

Put R=k^2, c=(R/2,0), r=R/2-4, and, for j=0,...,k-1, put t_j=j/R and

    p_j = R * ((1-t_j^2)/(1+t_j^2), 2*t_j/(1+t_j^2)).

These rational points have norm R. For the interior define

    lambda = 1+1/R^2,
    h = (floor(sqrt(3*R^4))+1)/(2*R^2),
    L = {c + lambda*(i+j/2, h*j): i,j integers},
    z_- = c+(0,-1/2),   z_+ = c+(0,1/2).

Take I to consist of z_-,z_+ and every lattice point in the closed radius-r
disk about c whose distance from each z_-,z_+ is strictly greater than 1.
Finally set

    A_k = {0} union {p_j: 0<=j<k} union I,
    s = 1-1/(8R),
    B_k = {s*p_j: 0<=j<k} union a labeled copy of I.

All formulas and disk tests have rational coordinates or rational squared
distances; the floor is an integer square-root computation. No numerical
optimality assumption is involved.

### Separation and the complete diameter graph

Since h>=sqrt(3)/2, a nonzero lattice difference has squared norm at least

    lambda^2*(i^2+i*j+j^2) >= lambda^2 > 1.

The inserted pair z_-,z_+ is at distance exactly 1. Its distances to all
retained lattice labels exceed 1 by construction. Thus I has exactly one
unit contact.

Since t_j<1/k, the circle chord formula gives, for j!=l,

    |p_j-p_l| = 2*|j-l|/sqrt((1+t_j^2)*(1+t_l^2)),
    32/17 <= |p_j-p_l| <= 2*(k-1) < R.

The bound 32/17 uses k>=4. Also

    R-p_(j,x) = 2*R*t_j^2/(1+t_j^2) <= 2,
    R/2 <= |p_j-c| <= R/2+2.

Consequently every leaf/interior distance belongs to [4,R-2]. Every
origin/interior distance belongs to [4,R-4], and every interior/interior
distance is at most R-8. These estimates verify every source pair type.
The only pairs at distance R are 0-p_j, so H is exactly the k-leaf star.
The only unit contact is z_--z_+; in particular the origin, every diameter
endpoint, and all other interior labels are contact isolated.

### Complete comparison and mixed-packet pair ledger

Each leaf moves a distance exactly 1/8. Its separation from interior labels
is therefore at least 31/8; its distances from noncorresponding old leaves
are at least 32/17-1/8>1. Distances between new leaves are at least
s*(32/17)>1. All upper cross conflicts are absent:

- old/new leaf distances are at most 2*(k-1)+1/8<R;
- old leaf/interior distances are at most R-2;
- new leaf/interior distances are at most R-15/8;
- origin/new leaf distances are exactly R-1/8;
- the other types have the earlier upper bounds R-4 and R-8.

Thus G has exactly the edges between each old leaf and its new copy, and
between each interior label and its coincident copy. All other cross
distances are in [1,R). In particular G is a matching, not just a planar
bounded-degree graph.

The packet {0} union B_k has |A_k| labels, minimum distance 1, and diameter
exactly R-1/8. The last equality follows because the origin/new leaf pairs
attain R-1/8 and every other pair type is strictly shorter. This directly
certifies nonglobality; these sources are not proposed counterexamples to
Erdős #99.

### The joint objective

The unique minimum-cardinality cover is T={0}. Every B label matches its
corresponding retained source label, so nu_T=m and the profit is -1.

The other inclusion-minimal cover consists of all k leaves. The origin has
no cross-conflict neighbor. Precisely the |I| old interior labels can be
matched, giving nu_T=|I|. Hence

    m-|T|-nu_T = (k+|I|)-k-|I| = 0.

These are the only two inclusion-minimal star covers. The monotonicity lemma
shows that all supersets have no better profit. Therefore the full union's
maximum feasible cardinality is exactly |A_k|, while the minimum-cover-first
search misses its genuine strict-D competitor.

### Population asymptotic

The fundamental parallelograms of L have area lambda^2*h and uniformly
bounded diameter, at most 3. Their tiling gives lower and upper disk counts
between pi*(r-3)^2/(lambda^2*h) and pi*(r+3)^2/(lambda^2*h), for r>=3.
Thus the disk population is pi*r^2/(lambda^2*h)+O(r).

At most 18 lattice labels are removed near the inserted pair: the disjoint
radius-1/2 disks about labels within distance 1 of either inserted point
fit in the union of two radius-3/2 disks, whose total area bounds the count
by 18. Since lambda^2*h=sqrt(3)/2+O(R^-2), the retained interior count is

    |I| = pi*(R/2-4)^2/(sqrt(3)/2)+O(R).

Adding k+1 labels gives the claimed triangular leading coefficient. The
O(D) error is retained; no exact optimum or improved population reserve is
claimed.

intervals, arbitrary vertical phase, averaging and `R`-to-`D/2` limit are valid.
Its separate lattice-defect, periodic and interface theorems are not premises

The contribution below is a quantitative strengthening of that boundary

## A stronger explicit linear reserve

**Classification: proved candidate awaiting independent human mathematical
review; unreviewed in the project lifecycle.**

Define the following exact constants:

\[
a={\sqrt3\over2},\quad h={56\over65},\quad
p=1-a,\quad q={98\over65}-a,\quad
b=a-q=\sqrt3-{98\over65},\quad k={9\over56},\quad C={65\over28},
\]
\[
s={256\over16385},\quad \beta={16383\over16385},
\qquad s^2+\beta^2=1,
\]
\[
\boxed{\gamma={6\over a}\{kb s-C(1-\beta)\}
 ={3(576b-65)\over114695a}
 =0.001939936045\ldots.}
\tag{L1}
\]

**Theorem.** For every real `R>=8192` a unit-separated finite packing in the
closed radius-`R` disk has population at least

\[
{\pi R^2\over a}+2\gamma R-{\sqrt R\over4}-60.
\tag{L2}
\]

Every global unit-separated `n`-point diameter minimizer with `D>16384` therefore
satisfies

\[
\boxed{g_A\ge\gamma D-{\sqrt D\over4\sqrt2}-60
             \ge\gamma D-{\sqrt D\over5}-60.}
\tag{L3}
\]

In particular,

\[
\boxed{D\ge10^6\quad\Longrightarrow\quad g_A\ge D/600.}
\tag{L4}
\]

The asymptotic linear coefficient exceeds PR #956's `1/320000` by a factor
greater than 620; the convenient effective coefficient `1/600` is greater by
exactly `1600/3`. Both are strictly stronger than any fixed `D^(2/3)`
coefficient asymptotically. The error in (L3) and its range are explicit.
This is not an assertion that `gamma` is best possible.

### Proof: one packet and simultaneous pair constraints

Let `f(z)=sqrt(R^2-z^2)`. Write a translated unit triangular lattice as
`{(t_x+j+l/2,t_y+la):j,l in Z}`. In each of the six coordinate frames obtained
by rotating through multiples of `pi/3`, select every lattice row at height

\[
\beta R\le y\le R-a.
\tag{L5}
\]

On its right side put
`u=f(y+a)`, `v=f(y+q)`, `ell=v-u`. Delete the lattice labels on that row in
`[u,v]` and insert

\[
(u+1+ih,\ y+\eta_i),\quad
0\le i\le\lfloor(\ell-2)/h\rfloor,\qquad
\eta_i=\begin{cases}p&i\text{ even},\\q&i\text{ odd}.\end{cases}
\tag{L6}
\]

Make the reflected replacement on the left. Since `q-p=33/65`, adjacent
inserted squared distances are exactly `h^2+(33/65)^2=1`; nonadjacent
horizontal distances are at least `2h>1`. Every old lower row has vertical
distance at least `a+p=1`. Every retained point of the same row is at
horizontal distance at least one. Every old higher-row point of the disk
has horizontal coordinate at most `u` on the right, or lies on the left,
so has horizontal separation at least one from a right packet. The left
version follows by reflection. Thus **all** new/old lower constraints hold;
the possible vertical equality at a lower row is allowed.

All new points lie in the original disk: their positive heights are at most
`y+q` and their horizontal coordinates lie in `[u+1,v-1]`, so in particular
have absolute value strictly below `f(y+q)`. Also

\[
\ell=\int_{y+q}^{y+a}{z\over f(z)}\,dz\ge b\beta/s>14>2.
\tag{L7}
\]

The packets are well defined. If `y_2>=y_1+a`, then
`v_(y_2)=f(y_2+q)<f(y_1+a)=u_(y_1)`. Hence two right packets of the same
frame are separated horizontally by more than two. A right packet and a
left packet have horizontal separation at least two. This covers all pairs
within one frame, even if their vertical ranges overlap.

Every inserted point is in the cone `|x|<=sR, y>=beta R` of its frame, and
has radius at least `beta R`. Different frame normals differ by at least
`pi/3`. With `phi=arcsin(s)`, their angular separation is at least
`pi/3-2phi`, so their distance is at least

\[
2\beta R\sin(\pi/6-\phi)
=\beta R(\beta-\sqrt3s)>R/2>1.
\tag{L8}
\]

For unequal radii this lower bound follows from
`|x-y|^2=(r_1-r_2)^2+4r_1r_2 sin^2(angle/2)`.
The same cone bound keeps different-frame deleted row intervals disjoint.
If two same-frame deletion intervals happen to share a boundary label,
counting it twice only overestimates deletions, which is safe. Thus all
twelve families can be performed together. Unchanged old pairs retain
triangular-lattice separation. This checks the whole packing, not just
individually feasible replacements.

### Proof: translation averaging without endpoint-rounding losses

Average the lattice translation over a fundamental domain. In a given frame,
conditional on its vertical phase, the horizontal row phase is uniform
modulo one. The expected number deleted from `[u,v]` is exactly `ell`;
closed endpoints affect a null set. The inserted count is
`K(y)=floor((ell-2)/h)+1 >= (ell-2)/h`.
Unfolding the vertical phase then gives expected gain, for all twelve
families combined, at least

\[
{12\over a}\int_{\beta R}^{R-a}\{k\ell(y)-C\}\,dy.
\tag{L9}
\]

The six frames are automorphisms of the triangular lattice. Their rotated
translation classes have the same uniform distribution; no independence
between frames is needed. The base crop population has expectation
`pi R^2/a`. All functions here are bounded and measurable on a compact
translation domain. An integer output at least its mean exists.

Put `I=integral_(beta R)^(R-a)ell(y)dy`. Substitution in the two terms gives
the exact telescoping identity

\[
I=\int_{\beta R+q}^{\beta R+a}f(z)\,dz
       -\int_{R-b}^R f(z)\,dz.
\tag{L10}
\]

The first term is at least `b f(beta R+a)` since `f` decreases. The second
is at most `(2/3)sqrt(2R)b^(3/2)`, since `f(R-t)<=sqrt(2Rt)`.
For `R>=8192` we have `beta R+a<=R` and

\[
f(\beta R+a)\ge sR-{2\beta a\over s}-{a^2\over sR},
\tag{L11}
\]

by `sqrt(X-e)>=sqrt(X)-e/sqrt(X)` for `0<=e<=X`.
Combining (L9)--(L11) and dropping the positive term `12C` gives expected
population at least

\[
{\pi R^2\over a}+2\gamma R-A\sqrt R-B_0,
\quad A={8\sqrt2\over a}k b^{3/2},\quad
B_0={12\over a}kb\left({2\beta a\over s}+{a^2\over8192s}\right).
\tag{L12}
\]

Exact arithmetic gives `A<1/4`, `B_0<60`, and `gamma>193/100000`.
These are inequalities between elements of `Q(sqrt(3))` after squaring
the positive `A` comparison. The reproducible verifier checks them with
integer/rational sign predicates. This proves (L2), with no discrepancy
theorem and for every real radius in the stated range.

### Proof: every global minimizer and the effective threshold

For a global `n`-point minimizer at `D>16384`, apply (L2) at **each**
`8192<=R<D/2`. Its integer competitor population is at most `n-1` because
its diameter is at most `2R<D`. Let `R` increase to `D/2`; only the continuous
numerical lower bound is passed to a limit. No diameter-`D` competitor is
used in the contradiction. This proves (L3).

For `x=sqrt(D)>=1000`,

\[
\left({193\over100000}-{1\over600}\right)x^2-{x\over5}-60
={79\over300000}x^2-{x\over5}-60>0.
\]

At `x=1000` this is `10/3`, and its derivative is positive for all
`x>=1000`. This proves (L4). All source labels and original lower constraints
are retained in the cardinality comparison; no lattice structure is imposed
on a minimizer. QED.

**Effective confirmation of the original coefficient.** The exact inequality
`kappa0<2/3` follows by cubing: `kappa0^3=243 pi^3/(32000a)` and the classical
bound `pi<22/7` suffices. Thus (L4), for `D>=64000000=400^3`, gives

\[
g_A\ge D/600\ge(2/3)D^{2/3}>\kappa_0D^{2/3}.
\tag{L13}
\]

This supplies an elementary effective proof of the headline bound with
**zero** remainder on this explicit range, independently of any effective
Huxley constant. It does not repair a flaw in Audit.243: its proof is valid.
The new input is a stronger, nonlattice comparison packing.

### Level I attempt and rigorous stopping point

The natural attempted bridge is to upper-bound the reserve of a triangle-free
global minimizer using its contact graph or a source lattice realization. The
new comparison supplies a larger boundary budget, but still supplies no such
realization. The remaining sufficient implication can be stated quantitatively:

\[
\text{every sufficiently large triangle-free global minimizer has}
\quad g_A\le cD+o(D)\quad\text{for some fixed }c<\gamma.
\tag{GAP}
\]

An admissible source-specific replacement of all `n` labels with strict diameter
improvement would also suffice. Neither implication was proved in this session.

There is a rigorous obstruction to dropping global optimality from (GAP).
Choose any `0<c<gamma`. By (L2), for every sufficiently large `D`, a disk of
radius `R=D/2-epsilon_D` with positive `epsilon_D` sufficiently small contains
at least `pi D^2/(4a)+cD` labels. For this *finite* packing, stretch its vertical
coordinate by `1+eta`, with `eta>0` small enough that `2R(1+eta)<D`. Every
distance weakly increases, and every old unit pair with a nonzero vertical
component becomes longer than one. Remaining unit edges are horizontal, and
three distinct collinear points cannot be mutually unit-separated by equality.
The contact graph is triangle-free. Untouched central lattice rows include
horizontal unit pairs, so the minimum distance remains exactly one. Its actual
diameter is below `D`. In terms of its actual diameter `d`, its population
excess `N-1-pi d^2/(4a)` is at least `c d` after choosing a slightly larger
intermediate coefficient between `c` and `gamma` to absorb the `-1`.
This is a feasible-source regression, not a sequence of global minimizers.

Thus neither arbitrary triangle-free density nor an independently constructed
triangular-lattice crop can be identified with the original source. This
session provides no new source-realization theorem. **Level I remains open.**

`STILL OPEN`

MC excludes the exact perfect-matching diameter graph. This report proves the quantitative stability theorem suggested by that closure: a post-ZF survivor cannot even be **sublinearly close** to a diameter matching.

Let

\[
\boxed{r_H:=2h-q
=\sum_{b\in B_+}(\deg_H(b)-1)
=x_B+Q+2s_Z.}
\tag{NM.1}
\]

Then every sufficiently large post-ZF survivor satisfies the exact finite inequality

\]

Consequently

\[
\boxed{
r_H\ge\frac{\lceil D\rceil-2}{3},}

\]

\[

\liminf_{D\to\infty}\frac{r_H}{D}
\ge\frac{2\rho}{3}
=0.4927234221\ldots ,
}
\tag{NM.4}
\]

where `rho` is the positive solution of `rho=cos rho`.

\[
2h-q=o(D)
\]

is completely eliminated. The post-ZF diameter graph must carry a definite linear amount of degree excess above a perfect matching.

## 1. Outer-walk excess localizes bad hull intervals

Write the loaded force-hull vertices in cyclic order as

\[
b_1,\ldots,b_q.
\]

The outer contact-face boundary walk encounters these extreme vertices in the same cyclic order, possibly with repeated vertices/bridge excursions between consecutive hull vertices. Choose one cyclic pass and split the outer walk into `q` subwalks

\[
W_i:b_i\leadsto b_{i+1}.
\]

Let `ell_i` be the number of contact-edge occurrences in `W_i`. Every consecutive hull pair is distinct and every contact path has at least one edge, so

\[
ell_i\ge1.
\]

Since

\[
b=q+x_B,
\]

we have

\[
\sum_{i=1}^q(\ell_i-1)=x_B.
\tag{1.1}
\]

Call `W_i` **good** if `ell_i=1` and **bad** otherwise. Let `m_bad` be the number of bad intervals. Then

\[
m_{bad}\le x_B.
\tag{1.2}
\]

The total number of outer-walk edge occurrences lying in bad intervals is

\[
\sum_{W_i\ bad}\ell_i
=m_{bad}+\sum_{W_i\ bad}(\ell_i-1)
\le2x_B.
\tag{1.3}
\]

If `W_i` is good, its unique edge joins two consecutive vertices of the convex force hull. The straight segment between those vertices is the hull side itself. Hence every good interval is one **unit convex-hull side contact**.

Thus at most `2x_B` outer-face edge incidences can be train ends that are not on good unit hull sides.

---

## 2. Exact exceptional-face train-end count

Let

- `f` be the number of bounded nonquadrilateral contact faces;
- `Q=sum_F(deg F-4)` over those faces;
- `g_F=sum_F(deg F-5)`.

Then

\[
Q=f+g_F.
\tag{2.1}
\]

The total boundary length of all exceptional bounded faces is not merely bounded by `5Q`; it is exactly

\[
\boxed{
L_{exc}:=\sum_{F\ exc}\deg F
=5f+g_F.
}
\tag{2.2}
\]

Every rhombic train end not on the outer contact face lies on an edge incident to a bounded nonquadrilateral face. Counting by face incidences therefore gives at most

\[
5f+g_F
\tag{2.3}
\]

such bad train-end incidences.

---

## 3. At most two trains can have two good convex-hull ends

Call a rhombic train **good** if both of its terminal edges are good unit hull-side contacts from Section 1.

C77 proves every train has one fixed unoriented edge direction; hence the two boundary ends of a good train are parallel unit hull sides.

A strict convex polygon has strictly increasing oriented edge direction around its boundary. Therefore an oriented edge direction occurs at most once, and an unoriented direction occurs at most twice, once in each opposite orientation. It follows that:

1. the two ends of one good train are an opposite-oriented parallel pair;
2. two distinct good trains have distinct unoriented directions.

Take two good trains with projective directions represented by

\[
0\le\theta_i<\theta_j<\pi.
\]

Their four oriented hull-side directions occur cyclically as

\[
\theta_i,
\theta_j,
\theta_i+\pi,
\theta_j+\pi.
\tag{3.1}
\]

Hence their two pairs of boundary edges alternate around the convex hull.

Represent the train tracks by C77's embedded simple dual arcs connecting the midpoints of their two terminal edges. Two disjoint arcs in a disk cannot connect alternating boundary pairs. Therefore every two good trains cross.

C77 says the train-intersection graph is triangle-free. Thus there cannot be three pairwise-crossing good trains.

### Lemma NM.1

\[
\boxed{
T_{good}\le2.
}
\tag{3.2}
\]

This is the stable form of the complete-crossing argument used in MC.

---

## 4. Every other train consumes a bad end

C77 proves every train has exactly two boundary ends. A train that is not good has at least one end either

1. on an outer-face edge occurrence belonging to a bad hull interval; or
2. on a bounded exceptional-face edge.

By (1.3) and (2.3), the total number of available bad train-end incidences is at most

\[
2x_B+5f+g_F.
\tag{4.1}
\]

Different train ends are distinct track states, so charging each nongood train to one bad end gives

\[
T-T_{good}
\le2x_B+5f+g_F.
\]

Using `T_good<=2`,

\[
\boxed{
T-2\le2x_B+5f+g_F.
}
\tag{4.2}

This is the key stability inequality.

---

DT and ZE give the exact train count

\[
T=\frac{b+Q}{2}+2f
=h-s_Z+2f.
\tag{5.1}
\]

Insert this into (4.2):

\[
h-s_Z+2f-2

Therefore

\[

\[

## 162.1 Common container data

Every Type-I macroscopic inactive-container survivor has an actual convex container `C_*`, internal or exterior, with an assigned contact-isolated source set `Z_*` such that

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{area}(C_*)=\Omega(D^2),

\operatorname{per}(C_*)=O(D),
\quad
\sigma_*=O(D).
}
\tag{162.1}
\]

For an internal chamber this is canonical. For a macroscopic exterior cap, canonical §80 gives constants `alpha,P_0,zeta>0` with

\[
\operatorname{area}(C)\ge\alpha D^2,
\qquad
\operatorname{per}(C)\le P_0D,
\qquad
|Z_C|\ge\zeta D^2.
\tag{162.2}
\]

The cap convention uses

\[
\sigma_C^{ext}
={\operatorname{area}(C)\over a_0}
+{\operatorname{per}(C)\over2}-1-|Z_C|,
\qquad a_0={\sqrt3\over2},

whereas the isolate-only matching theorem uses

\[
\sigma_C
={\operatorname{area}(C)\over a_0}
+{\operatorname{per}(C)\over2}+1-|Z_C|.

\[
\boxed{\sigma_C=\sigma_C^{ext}+2=O(D).}

The difference is only the two closing-chord endpoint convention.

Canonical §80 supplies the exterior-cap geometry, population, slack, and the partition of `K\setminus F` into convex cap interiors up to closing chords. Hence a source point `z\notin F` cannot be incident to a unit contact: otherwise that actual contact lies in `C=C_*`, is positive in a relative-interior normalized stress, and places `z` in `V(G)\subset F`, a contradiction. Therefore every source point assigned to an exterior cap is contact-isolated in the chosen representative. The cap partition then implies that every source point not assigned to the selected cap lies outside `\operatorname{int}(C)`.

## 162.2 Linear inradius and fixed-depth cores

Fixed positive depth is therefore available in either Type-I geometry.

## 162.3 Strict unit covering and finite exchange saturation

For every sufficiently large survivor,

\[
\boxed{
C_{*,-1}
\subseteq
\bigcup_{z\in Z_*}\overline B(z,1).
}
\tag{162.6}

### Proof

Suppose `x in C_{*,-1}` were farther than one from every assigned isolate. Every source point outside `int(C_*)` is also farther than one from `x`: the segment from `x` to that point meets `partial C_*` at distance strictly greater than one.

Delete any nonisolated contact vertex `v` of the positive core and insert `x`. Cardinality is preserved, the new source is strictly unit-separated, and `x` remains in the old full source hull `K`, so its diameter is at most `D`. Global optimality forces the diameter to equal `D(n)`, while the old vertex `v` had at least one unit contact and the inserted point has none. This contradicts contact minimality. \(\square\)

More generally, for every finite `W subset Z_*`, there is no set

\[
Y\subset C_{*,-1},
\qquad |Y|=|W|+1,
\tag{162.7}

such that

\[
|y-y'|>1
\quad(y\ne y'\in Y),
\qquad
|y-z|>1
\quad(y\in Y,\ z\in Z_*\setminus W).
\tag{162.8}
\]

Indeed every retained source outside the container interior is protected by depth, so replacing `W` together with one nonisolated core vertex by `Y` would produce a same-cardinality global minimizer with fewer contacts.

Thus either Type-I container is finitely exchange-saturated in the same strict sense.

## 1. Projective separation of all actual diameter directions

Let `H` be the full actual diameter graph of the canonical C-II source and let `D` be the source diameter. Put

\[
a_D:=\arcsin\frac1{2D},
\qquad
\delta_D:=2a_D.
\]

We first re-prove the only C67 input needed below.

### Lemma DB.1 — shared-endpoint separation

If `ba` and `bc` are distinct diameter edges sharing `b`, and `theta=angle abc`, then

\[
|a-c|=2D\sin(\theta/2).
\]

Unit separation gives `|a-c|>=1`, hence

\[
\boxed{\theta\ge\delta_D.}
\tag{DB.1}
\]

Also `|a-c|<=D`, so `theta<=pi/3`. Thus `theta` is exactly the projective circular distance between the two supporting line directions.

### Lemma DB.2 — disjoint-edge separation

Let `AB` and `CD` be vertex-disjoint diameter edges. The planar diameter graph is a straight-line thrackle, so the two segments cross properly. Let `phi in (0,pi/2]` be the acute angle between their supporting lines.

Place

\[
A=(0,0),\qquad B=(D,0),
\]

and label the second chord

\[
C=(x,-u),\qquad D'=(y,v),
\]

with `u,v>0` and `x<=y`. Because every source point is within distance `D` of both `A` and `B`,

\[
0\le x\le y\le D.
\]

The horizontal and vertical components of the length-`D` chord are

\[
y-x=D\cos\phi,
\qquad
u+v=D\sin\phi.
\]

Set

\[
s:=x+(D-y)=D(1-\cos\phi)
={D\sin^2\phi\over1+\cos\phi}.
\]

Suppose `D sin(phi)<1`. For `D>=2`, this gives `s<1/2`. Since `0<=x<=s` and `0<=D-y<=s`, unit separation of `C` from `A` and of `D'` from `B` gives

\[
u^2+x^2\ge1,
\qquad
v^2+(D-y)^2\ge1,
\]

hence

\[
u>\sqrt{1-s^2}>{\sqrt3\over2},
\qquad
v>{\sqrt3\over2}.
\]

Thus `u+v>sqrt(3)>1`, contradicting `u+v=D sin(phi)<1`. Therefore

\[
\phi\ge\arcsin(1/D)>\delta_D.
\tag{DB.2}
\]

Combining the two cases, distinct actual diameter edges have distinct projective directions with pairwise projective circular distance at least

\[
\boxed{\delta_D=2\arcsin{1\over2D}.}
\tag{DB.3}
\]

No KKT weights occur in this statement.

## 2. The diameter direction polygon in the difference body

\[

\[

=4D\sum_{i=1}^h\sin{g_i\over2},

## 6. Canonical near half-turn symmetry of the full actual force hull

The universal full-source theorem `C-FS-GEOM` applies to every selected stress. On the canonical lexicographic C-II source choose a relative-interior normalized stress. Its positive diameter support is the full actual `H=H_*`, so its selected force hull is precisely the full actual force hull `F` used above.

Let `o` be the full-source circumcenter and put

\[
F_0:=F-o,
\qquad
L_D:=\sqrt{D\eta+\eta^2},
\qquad
\eta=3^{1/4}\sqrt D.
\]

The canonical half-turn estimate is

\[
\boxed{d_H(F_0,-F_0)\le2L_D,}
\qquad
L_D=O(D^{3/4})=o(D).
\tag{DB.21}
\]

Set `epsilon_D=2L_D`. Then

\[
-F_0\subseteq F_0+\epsilon_DB_2,
\]

so

\[
F-F=F_0+(-F_0)
\subseteq2F_0+\epsilon_DB_2.
\]

Steiner's formula and `per(F)<=pi D` give the finite bound

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{area}(F-F)
\le
4\operatorname{area}(F)
+2\epsilon_D\operatorname{per}(F)
+\pi\epsilon_D^2.
}
\tag{DB.22}
\]

The last two terms are `o(D^2)`. Thus the generic planar Rogers–Shephard factor six improves on this source to the asymptotic centrally symmetric factor four:

\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{area}(F-F)
\le4\operatorname{area}(F)+o(D^2).
}
\tag{DB.23}
\]

The factor four is sharp for centrally symmetric `F`.

## 7. Symmetry-corrected force-hull area floor

By DB.5, DB.7, DB.11, and DB.22,

\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{area}(F)
\ge{}&{D^2\over4}
\left[(h-1)\sin(2a_D)+\sin(2(h-1)a_D)\right]\\
&-{\epsilon_D\over2}\operatorname{per}(F)
-{\pi\over4}\epsilon_D^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{DB.24}
\]

Along a subsequence with `h/D->y`, the error is `o(D^2)` and

\[
(h-1)\sin(2a_D)\to y,
\qquad
2(h-1)a_D\to y.
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\liminf{\operatorname{area}(F)\over D^2}
\ge A_{sym}(y):={y+\sin y\over4}.
}
\tag{DB.25}
\]

On `[0,pi]`, `A_sym'(y)=(1+cos y)/4>=0`. Combining with DB.19 gives the universal post-ZF force-hull area floor

\[
\boxed{
\liminf{\operatorname{area}(F)\over D^2}
\ge
A_{SC}:={2\rho+\sin(2\rho)\over4}
=0.6184708847696858\ldots .
}
\tag{DB.26}
\]

The isodiametric maximum is `pi/4`, so this leaves at most

\[
\left({\pi\over4}-A_{SC}+o(1)\right)D^2
=
(0.1669272786277625\ldots+o(1))D^2
\]

of force-hull area deficit.

This does not imply that the full source population outside `F` is subquadratic.

## 8. A common-center force-hull inradius floor

Let

\[
g_{max}:=\max_i g_i.
\]

Because every other gap is at least `2a_D`,

\[
\boxed{g_{max}\le\pi-2(h-1)a_D.}
\tag{DB.27}
\]

The vertices of `P_H/2` lie on the radius-`D/2` circle. For a centrally symmetric inscribed polygon, the centered inradius is the distance to the side subtending the largest angular gap:

\[
r(P_H/2)={D\over2}\cos(g_{max}/2).
\]

Hence DB.27 gives

\[
\boxed{
B\!\left(0,{D\over2}\sin((h-1)a_D)\right)
\subseteq {1\over2}P_H.
}
\tag{DB.28}
\]

From DB.5 and DB.21,

\[
P_H\subseteq F-F
\subseteq2(F-o)+2L_DB_2.
\]

Dividing by two,

\[
{1\over2}P_H\subseteq(F-o)+L_DB_2.
\]

Support functions and DB.28 therefore give

\[
\boxed{
B\!\left(
o,
{D\over2}\sin((h-1)a_D)-L_D
\right)
\subseteq F
}
\tag{DB.29}
\]

whenever the displayed radius is positive.

Along `h/D->y`,

\[
\liminf {r_o(F)\over D}
\ge{1\over2}\sin(y/2),
\]

where `r_o(F)` is the largest disk centered at the common source circumcenter and contained in `F`. Using DB.19 and `y<=pi`,

\[
\boxed{
\liminf {r_o(F)\over D}
\ge{1\over2}\sin\rho
=0.3368060145916074\ldots .
}
\tag{DB.30}
\]

Thus the same point `o` simultaneously satisfies

\[
B(o,(0.336806\ldots-o(1))D)
\subseteq F
\subseteq K
\subseteq B(o,D/2+O(\sqrt D)).
\]

The annular completion region between these radii still has quadratic area. Ordinary area capacity alone therefore does not close the contact-isolated population branch.

## 9. Regression audit

### Regular odd shells

For regular odd shells, `h/D->pi`. Then

\[
A_{sym}(\pi)={\pi\over4},
\qquad
{1\over2}\sin(\pi/2)={1\over2}.
\]

The area and inradius statements converge to the exact disk limits, so the theorem does not falsely exclude the mandatory shell regression.

### Dense isolated fillings

The proof never sets `n=v`, never removes contact-isolated source points, and never bounds their number. They can remain KKT-invisible while the force hull satisfies DB.26–DB.30.

### Response weights

Every statement in Sections 1–5 is weight-free. Sections 6–8 use only the canonical geometric half-turn estimate. No lower bound on an individual or aggregate `beta` weight is inferred.

### No trace/operator shortcut

The odd-shell response regression from `58-full-source-geometry-audit.md` remains binding. The area and inradius floors do not imply a small response trace defect, an operator-norm estimate, or an almost-full-weight matching.

The post-ZF full actual force hull now has a stronger quantitative normal form:

\boxed{
{h\over D}\ge2\rho-o(1),
\qquad
{\operatorname{per}(F)\over D}\ge4\rho-o(1),
}
\]

\[
\boxed{
{\operatorname{area}(F)\over D^2}
\ge0.6184708847696858\ldots-o(1),
}
\]

and, around the same full-source circumcenter,

\[
\boxed{
{r_o(F)\over D}
\ge0.3368060145916074\ldots-o(1).
}
\]

These statements sharply restrict the geometry available to both Woodall branches. They do not close either branch. A successful continuation still needs a source-capacity loss, an upper restriction crossing the canonical surplus floors, or a strict sub-`D` competitor. # Target C — linear nonmatching-excess audit

This module independently audits the old near-matching train argument and then combines
it with the now-canonical defect-sensitive difference-body inequality. It strengthens
the exact perfect-matching exclusion to a quantitative theorem with a fixed positive
linear constant.

It does not assume `s_Z=0`, does not use a KKT weight floor, and does not discard
contact-isolated source points.

**LEVEL I STATUS: STILL OPEN. C-II REMAINS OPEN.**

# 61. Linear diameter branching above the matching endpoint

Work with the canonical contact-minimal, then diameter-pair-minimal C-II source. Let

- `D` be its diameter;
- `q` be the number of loaded diameter vertices;
- `h` be the number of actual loaded diameter edges;
- `d_H=q-h`;
- `b` be the outer contact-face boundary-walk length, with multiplicity;
- `x_B=b-q`;
- `Q=sum_F(deg F-4)` over bounded nonquadrilateral contact faces;
- `f` be the number of those nonquadrilateral faces;
- `g_F=sum_F(deg F-5)`, so `Q=f+g_F`; and
- `s_Z=e+h-(2v-2)>=0` be the canonical post-ZF mixed-rigidity surplus.

Define the **nonmatching excess**

\[
\boxed{r_H:=2h-q.}
\tag{61.1}
\]

The main conclusions are the exact finite inequality

\[
\boxed{3r_H\ge h-2,}
\tag{61.2}
\]

and the sharper asymptotic theorem

\[
\boxed{
\liminf_{D\to\infty}{r_H\over D}\ge c_*,
\qquad
c_* = \cos\!\left({3c_*\over2}\right),
\qquad
0.6099<c_*<0.61.
}
\tag{61.3}
\]

The root `c_*` is unique in `(0,1)`; numerically it is approximately
`0.6099043189`.

In the Woodall forest branch, if the caterpillar components have vertex counts
`q_1,...,q_{d_H}`, then

\[
r_H=q-2d_H=\sum_{j=1}^{d_H}(q_j-2).
\tag{61.4}
\]

Thus every sufficiently large forest survivor has a fixed linear amount of aggregate
caterpillar excess beyond disjoint matching edges.

## 61.1 Exact defect identity

Euler plus canonical ZF gives

\[
{b+Q\over2}=h-s_Z.
\tag{61.5}
\]

Since `b=q+x_B`,

\[
q+x_B+Q=2h-2s_Z.
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{
r_H=2h-q=x_B+Q+2s_Z
=x_B+f+g_F+2s_Z.
}
\tag{61.6}
\]

This is the exact currency identity used throughout the proof.

## 61.2 Finite stopped-rhombus trains

We re-prove the train facts needed below rather than importing the old unreviewed
campaign theorem.

Every bounded quadrilateral contact face is a simple convex unit rhombus by the
canonical face theorem. Triangle-freeness forces both diagonals to exceed one, so its
acute projective side-angle lies strictly in `(pi/3,pi/2]`.

Make the train-link graph whose vertices are contact edges. Each bounded rhombus adds
two links, joining each pair of opposite sides. Every train-link vertex has degree at
most two. Along one connected train all transverse contact edges have one fixed
projective direction. Orient that direction as `u` and orient passage through each
rhombus toward the same normal `Ju`. Every midpoint step then makes angle strictly
less than `pi/6` with `Ju`, so projection onto `Ju` increases strictly. Therefore a
train cannot close into a cycle; every train is a path, with a singleton contact edge
allowed.

If two trains cross in a rhombus, the acute projective separation `delta` of their
transverse directions is greater than `pi/3`. Orient their normals with angle `delta`.
Each train's midpoint path has all step directions in an open cone of half-angle
`pi/6` about its normal. In coordinates along the bisector of the two normals, both
paths are piecewise-linear graphs and their slope intervals are disjoint and ordered.
Their height difference is therefore strictly monotone, so two trains cross at most
once.

Three trains cannot cross pairwise: three projective directions on a circle of length
`pi` cannot have all three cyclic gaps greater than `pi/3`. Thus the train-crossing
graph is simple and triangle-free.

Let `R` be the number of bounded quadrilateral faces and `T` the number of trains,
including isolated contact-edge trains. The train-link graph has `e` vertices and
`2R` links and is a forest, so

\[
T=e-2R.
\]

Face incidence gives

\[
2e=4R+b+\sum_{F\text{ non4}}\deg F.
\]

Since

\[
\sum_{F\text{ non4}}\deg F=5f+g_F=4f+Q,
\]

we obtain

\[
\boxed{
T={b+Q\over2}+2f=h-s_Z+2f.
}
\tag{61.7}
\]

The second equality uses (61.5).

The argument allows bridges, repeated outer-walk occurrences, disconnected rhombic
regions, and arbitrary bounded exceptional faces.

## 61.3 Bad outer train ends cost at most `2x_B`

List the loaded force-hull vertices in cyclic order as

\[
b_1,\ldots,b_q.
\]

Choose their distinguished exterior occurrences on the outer contact-face boundary
walk. They occur in the same cyclic order. Split that cyclic walk into `q` subwalks

\[
W_i:b_i\leadsto b_{i+1}
\]

and let `ell_i` be the number of contact-edge occurrences in `W_i`. Then

\[
ell_i\ge1,
\qquad
\sum_i\ell_i=b=q+x_B,
\]

so

\[
\sum_i(\ell_i-1)=x_B.
\tag{61.8}
\]

Call `W_i` good if `ell_i=1` and bad otherwise. The number of bad intervals is at
most `x_B`, and the total number of outer-walk edge occurrences in bad intervals is

\[
\sum_{W_i\,\mathrm{bad}}\ell_i
\le x_B+x_B
=2x_B.
\tag{61.9}
\]

A good interval is one unit contact edge joining consecutive convex-hull vertices,
so it is exactly a unit force-hull side.

Therefore at most `2x_B` outer-face train-end incidences fail to lie on good unit hull
sides.

## 61.4 Exceptional train ends cost exactly `5f+g_F`

Every train end that is not on the outer face lies on an edge incident to a bounded
nonquadrilateral face. Their total face-incidence capacity is

\[
\boxed{
\sum_{F\text{ non4}}\deg F=5f+g_F.
}
\tag{61.10}
\]

This is an upper bound on the number of such train-end incidences, including singleton
trains between two exceptional faces.

## 61.5 At most two trains have two good hull ends

Call a train **good** if both of its terminal incidences are good unit force-hull side
contacts.

The two terminal edges of one train are parallel because opposite sides remain
parallel throughout the train. Their oriented hull directions are opposite. Strict
convexity makes the oriented side direction increase strictly around the hull, so one
unoriented direction appears at most twice.

Take two distinct good trains with projective directions represented by

\[
0\le\theta_i<\theta_j<\pi.
\]

Their four oriented hull-side directions occur cyclically as

\[
\theta_i,\ \theta_j,\ \theta_i+\pi,\ \theta_j+\pi.
\tag{61.11}
\]

Thus the endpoint pairs alternate on the boundary of the convex disk `F`.

The midpoint realization of each train is an embedded simple arc: strict monotone
projection from Section 61.2 rules out self-intersection. Two disjoint arcs in a disk
cannot join alternating boundary pairs. Hence every two good trains cross.

But the train-crossing graph is triangle-free. Therefore

\[
\boxed{T_{\rm good}\le2.}
\tag{61.12}
\]

This is the topological step that turns train geometry into quantitative diameter
branching.

## 61.6 Exact near-matching inequality

Every nongood train consumes at least one bad end. By (61.9), (61.10), and (61.12),

\[
T-2\le2x_B+5f+g_F.
\tag{61.13}
\]

Insert the exact train count (61.7):

\[
h-s_Z+2f-2
\le2x_B+5f+g_F,
\]

so

\[
\boxed{
h-2\le2x_B+3f+g_F+s_Z.}
\tag{61.14}
\]

Multiply (61.6) by three. Since

\[
3r_H-(2x_B+3f+g_F+s_Z)
=x_B+2g_F+5s_Z\ge0,
\]

we obtain the exact finite theorem

\[
\boxed{3(2h-q)\ge h-2.}
\tag{61.15}
\]

In particular canonical ZR/ZF gives `h>=ceil(D)`, hence

\[
\boxed{
2h-q\ge{\lceil D\rceil-2\over3}.
}
\tag{61.16}
\]

So linear nonmatching topology already follows without any asymptotic area theorem.

## 61.7 Defect-sensitive DB sharpens the constant

Put

\[
z:=Q+2s_Z=f+g_F+2s_Z.
\tag{61.17}
\]

Then `r_H=x_B+z`. From (61.14),

\[
3f+g_F+s_Z\le3z,
\]

and therefore

\[
\boxed{h-2\le2r_H+z.}
\tag{61.18}
\]

The canonical Section 59 difference-body theorem gives the exact finite inequality

\[
\boxed{
z
\le h+1-2D\cos((h-1)a_D),
\qquad
a_D=\arcsin{1\over2D}.}
\tag{61.19}
\]

Substituting (61.19) into (61.18) and cancelling `h` gives

\[
\boxed{
r_H
\ge D\cos((h-1)a_D)-{3\over2}.}
\tag{61.20}
\]

Equation (61.15) also gives

\[
\boxed{r_H\ge{h-2\over3}.}
\tag{61.21}
\]

Because the loaded diameter graph is a planar diameter pseudoforest, `h<=q`, while
`q<=per(F)<=pi D`; hence `h/D` is bounded. Pass to any subsequence on which

\[
{h\over D}\to y.
\]

Since

\[
a_D={1\over2D}+O(D^{-3}),
\]

we have `(h-1)a_D -> y/2`. Divide (61.20)-(61.21) by `D`. Every subsequential limit
`r` of `r_H/D` obeys

\[
\boxed{
r\ge\max\left\{{y\over3},\cos{y\over2}\right\}.}
\tag{61.22}
\]

On `0<y<pi`, `y/3` increases strictly and `cos(y/2)` decreases strictly. Their
maximum is minimized at the unique crossover

\[
{y_*\over3}=\cos{y_*\over2}.
\tag{61.23}
\]

Set

\[
c_*:={y_*\over3}.
\]

Then

\[
\boxed{c_*=\cos(3c_*/2),}
\tag{61.24}
\]

and (61.22) yields

\[
\boxed{
\liminf {2h-q\over D}\ge c_*.
}
\tag{61.25}
\]

Uniqueness follows because

\[
F(c)=c-\cos(3c/2)
\]

has

\[
F'(c)=1+{3\over2}\sin(3c/2)>0
\]

for `0<c<1`, while `F(0)<0<F(1)`.

The registered exact certificate proves

\[
\boxed{0.6099<c_*<0.61}
\tag{61.26}
\]

using rational alternating Taylor bounds for cosine; no decimal transcendental
evaluation is used by the certificate.

## 61.8 Optimality for the two audited inequalities

The constant `c_*` is not an artifact of a loose rearrangement. For fixed normalized
edge density `y=h/D`, write normalized currencies

\[
x={x_B\over D},\quad
u={f\over D},\quad
g={g_F\over D},\quad
s={s_Z\over D}.
\]

Ignoring vanishing `O(1/D)` terms, the train-end inequality requires

\[
2x+3\nu+g+s\ge y,
\tag{61.27}
\]

while the DB defect capacity gives

\[
\nu+g+2s\le y-2\cos(y/2).
\tag{61.28}
\]

The branching cost is

\[
r=x+\nu+g+2s.
\tag{61.29}
\]

Among the DB-controlled currencies, `nu` supplies the most train-end capacity per unit
branching cost. Solving the resulting fixed-`y` linear relaxation gives

\[
\boxed{
r_{\min}(y)=\max\{y/3,\cos(y/2)\}.}
\tag{61.30}
\]

Thus `c_*` is the best universal constant obtainable from the audited train-end and DB
inequalities alone. A stronger constant requires new geometry, not algebraic
rearrangement.

## 61.9 Woodall interpretation

In the Woodall forest branch, `d_H` is exactly the number of caterpillar components,
and each component has at least two vertices. Since `h=q-d_H`,

\[
2h-q=q-2d_H
=\sum_j(q_j-2).
\tag{61.31}
\]

Therefore

\[
\boxed{
\liminf {1\over D}\sum_j(q_j-2)\ge c_*>0.6099.
}
\tag{61.32}
\]

This is much stronger than merely excluding a perfect matching. A survivor cannot
hide its nonmatching topology in finitely many bounded-size caterpillars or in an
`o(D)` aggregate perturbation of matching components.

The exact finite inequality also gives

\[
5d_H\le2q+2,
\tag{61.33}
\]

so asymptotically

\[
\boxed{{d_H\over q}\le{2\over5}+o(1).}
\tag{61.34}
\]

In the Woodall cyclic branch `d_H=0` and `r_H=q`; Section 61 is primarily a forest
stability theorem there.

## 61.10 Scope and regressions

- **Perfect matching:** `r_H=0`, so (61.15) permits only `h<=2`; the large perfect
  matching branch is subsumed by the stronger theorem.
- **Matching plus finitely many bounded caterpillars:** `r_H=O(1)`; excluded for
  unbounded `D`.
- **Matching plus `o(D)` aggregate caterpillar excess:** excluded.
- **Regular odd shell:** Woodall cyclic with `r_H=q`; fully compatible.
- **Positive `s_Z`:** retained and charged honestly through both (61.6) and DB.
- **Exceptional faces:** retained via their exact train-end incidence `5f+g_F`.
- **Bridge excursions / repeated outer walk:** retained via the exact `2x_B` bad-end
  bound.
- **Contact-isolated source points:** retained; none are identified with contact-core
  vertices.
- **KKT coefficient floors:** not used.
- **Rejected cyclic Reuleaux-cap containment:** not used.

## 61.11 Remaining obstruction

Every forest survivor now has at least `c_*D-o(D)` aggregate caterpillar excess, but
this still does not force one giant caterpillar, a positive fraction of nontrivial
components, or positive KKT mass on the excess topology.

The next useful theorem should couple

\[
r_H=x_B+Q+2s_Z
\]

to the independently audited renormalized contact currency

\[
e_{BB}+2s_C-3(d_H+s_Z),
\]

or to the common bridge-block/negative-transfer structure, without double charging
`x_B`, `Q`, or `s_Z`.

## 8. What remains to be proved

The route can be sharpened into a precise research target:

Find a theorem tying exact global optimality to original contact structure, with quantitative control strong enough to exclude every triangle-free penny-graph configuration.

Two possible sufficient results would be especially consequential. One is a universal contact lower bound with coefficient strictly less than 122π3\frac12\sqrt{2\pi\sqrt3}21​2π3​​, allowing direct application of Eppstein. Another is a universal rigidity or stress-support theorem for a large interior region, together with an additional geometric argument excluding triangle-free rhombic networks at exactly DnD_nDn​.

The second approach must do more than show that rhombic angles tend to 60∘60^\circ60∘. It must prove that some original angle equals 60∘60^\circ60∘, or that every configuration with all such angles strictly larger admits a feasible diameter-decreasing deformation. Such a deformation must account for all original unit constraints and all active diametral constraints simultaneously.

The high-contact rhombic construction shows why this last step is subtle: the interior may have only an O(1)O(1)O(1) total angular defect while every prospective equilateral-triangle diagonal remains strictly longer than one. An O(1)O(1)O(1) diameter gap is precisely the scale at which asymptotic packing estimates cease to distinguish these competitors from an exact optimum.

## Final assessment

The Oler-to-saturation approach produces a strong global shape theorem and a meaningful rigidity-based conditional edge bound, but it does not currently prove that every sufficiently large original global optimizer contains a unit equilateral triangle.

The strongest identified obstruction is the near-triangular rhombic family: it has a circular hull to bounded error, optimal leading diameter, 2n−O(n)2n-O(\sqrt n)2n−O(n​) exact original contacts, and arbitrarily small angular defects, yet no original unit triangle. The missing distinction is its uncertified O(1)O(1)O(1) excess diameter.

Conversely, no infinite sequence of rigorously certified globally optimal triangle-free original configurations has been obtained here. Erdős Problem 99 remains open.

- Exact global countermodel: At n=8n=8n=8, globally optimal configurations can have 7 or 9 unit contacts while possessing exactly the same convex hull, area, perimeter and diameter. One is triangle-free; the other contains a unit equilateral triangle.
- Quantitative obstruction: For every nnn and every positive tolerance, there are feasible, triangle-free configurations with exactly one unit contact and diameter arbitrarily close to the exact global minimum.
- Area–perimeter result: Oler's inequality, combined with an explicit triangular-lattice covering argument, gives a bounded hull-perimeter deficit of asymptotically at most 7π/(23)≈6.357\pi/(2\sqrt3)\approx6.357π/(23​)≈6.35. This still gives no lower bound on exact contacts.
- Stress obstruction: An explicit positive equilibrium stress exists for the globally optimal triangle-free n=8n=8n=8 configuration, yet its interior point has no contacts and no positive stress support.

These results defeat several plausible auxiliary hypotheses, but none is an infinite family of triangle-free exact global optimizers.

## 8. The precise unresolved proof obligation

A satisfactory contact-count proof would need to establish a theorem of the following type.

For some ε>0\varepsilon>0ε>0 and sufficiently large nnn, every original globally optimal configuration AnA_nAn​ satisfies

### Final assessment
